narrative:
The model determined that you have a 39% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability crossed the threshold the bank uses, your loan application was denied.

Three pieces of information about you weighed most heavily in that decision. First, the fact that you have no savings account or an unknown savings status pulled the prediction strongly toward approval. This is actually a positive factor for you. Second, having other installment plans already running at a bank pushed the prediction noticeably toward rejection. Third, the status of your checking account also worked against you, though less strongly than the installment plans.

Your lack of savings should have helped your case, but it was more than offset by the combination of requesting a much larger loan (7,824 DM versus the 3,020 DM average for approved applicants) for 28 months instead of the typical 19 months, along with your relatively short employment history of less than one year. These additional factors, together with your existing bank installment plan, made the overall picture look risky to the model.

You should focus on building savings, reducing your existing installment commitments if possible, and perhaps re-applying in a few months with a smaller loan amount or after you have been employed longer. This would remove the main elements that currently work against you.
